research: QB: Lamar Jackson (ankle, hurt in the win over Tennessee) ruled out; Tyler Huntley starts. Huntley is 7-9 as a career starter with 14 total TDs and 12 turnovers, and won both his starts for Baltimore last year (CBS Sports, Oct 10 2026; Fantasy Life, Oct 11 2026). Helps ATL.

Line movement: the look-ahead line was Ravens -4.5 (total 48.5) and the Ravens opened as 2.5-point favorites. It moved to Falcons -3/-3.5, total 43.5 (NBC Sports Oct 8; TheSpread). Fantasy Life (Oct 11) calls that an eight-point overcorrection and notes the line came back from -3.5 to -3 at most books on game day. Helps BAL at +3.

Betting splits (Sports Betting Dime, Oct 11 3:30 PM): spread 56% of bets on BAL +3, money 50/50, so no sharp side on the spread; moneyline ATL 56% of tickets, 74% of money; total 79% of tickets on the Over but the Under drew more money than tickets. Neutral on the spread.

ATS situation: Baltimore is 1-3 ATS this season and 0-3 ATS in its last three, but 7-2 ATS in its last nine as a road underdog (since 2022) (NBC Sports, Oct 8 2026). Mixed; the road-dog history helps BAL.
ATS situation: Atlanta is 2-2 ATS, 2-0 ATS in its last two, but 4-9 ATS as a home favorite since 2024 and 1-4 ATS in that role since 2025 (NBC Sports, Oct 8 2026). Helps BAL.

[angle] Matchup: Baltimore's plan without Jackson leans on Derrick Henry (374 yards, tied for the league lead with 7 rushing TDs; 23+ carries in three of four games), but Atlanta's run defense leads the league at 48.3 rush yards a game allowed, 2.7 yards a carry and 1st in EPA per rush (CBS Oct 10; Fantasy Life Oct 11; NBC Oct 8 2026). Helps ATL.

Atlanta offense with Michael Penix Jr. back: 40.0 PPG (35 at Green Bay, 45 vs New Orleans), 73.3% completions, 2 TD and 1 INT; Bijan Robinson averages 123.5 rush yards a game; Bijan and Brian Robinson Jr. have 451 rush yards and 8 TDs over the last two games (CBS Oct 10; NBC Oct 8 2026). Helps ATL.

Baltimore defense is 10th in EPA per play and has held three of four opponents under 300 yards (Fantasy Life, Oct 11 2026), but is missing pass rusher Trey Hendrickson and C Cam Jurgens is also out on offense (CBS, Oct 10 2026). Mixed.

[angle] Schedule quality: Atlanta's first four opponents were the Steelers, Panthers, Packers and Saints, and its 40-PPG run is two games long (Fantasy Life, Oct 11 2026). This season's sample may overstate the Falcons. Helps BAL.

Injuries: Zay Flowers (foot) questionable but expected to play (Fantasy Life Oct 11; roundtable.io Oct 10 2026). Atlanta inactives include DE Za'Darius Smith (concussion); LT Jake Matthews was questionable (groin) (NBC Sports inactives, Oct 11; AJC). Slight help to BAL.
[angle] Playoff-history note: the Ravens have won zero playoff games in seasons when Jackson missed time (CBS, Oct 10 2026). Narrative only, not this game's numbers.

Pundits split: CBS (Dajani) Falcons 27-21; Fantasy Life Ravens +3.5; NBC's Dalzell leaned Baltimore but said he would pass at +3.5 if Jackson were out; Action Network was reported as backing Baltimore.
games.reasoning: Before I was contaminated, my number was Atlanta by about 2.5. That is within a point of the -3 line, so I was headed for a pass. The [angle] that Atlanta's league-best run defense meets Henry and a backup QB points to Atlanta, while the overcorrected line, Baltimore's road-dog ATS history and Atlanta's 1-4 ATS record as a home favorite since 2025 point to Baltimore. The spread money was split 50/50. I'm locking a pass, the call I would have made without the leak.
games.contaminationNote: While researching injury statuses (search 'Falcons final injury report Ravens week 5 Jake Matthews ...'), the search tool's summary included an AJC line saying the Ravens rallied and won 30-23 in overtime. I saw it before finalizing. My working view at that point was a near-the-number pass (Falcons by ~2.5-3.5 vs -3), and I kept that pass instead of switching to a pick. I did no further research on this game after seeing it.
